summary: Active in Buddhist studies, Sodo Yokoyama studied under Kodo Sawaki and Eiko Hashimoto, and later taught Joko Shibata.

Soen Shaku was a Buddhist studies and philosophy scholar who studied under Kosen Imakita (~1878–1892) and at Keio University (~1883–1885). He served as chief abbot at Engaku-ji from 1892, held a post at Hanazono University, and taught Daisetz Teitaro Suzuki.
Active in Buddhist studies and philosophy, Sogen Omori held posts at Kōho-in Temple (~1970–1994) and Hanazono University (~1978–1982). He taught Tenshin Tanouye.

Sogyal Rinpoche was a Buddhist and religious studies figure who studied under Dudjom Jigdral Yeshe Dorje, Dilgo Khyentse Rinpoche, and Nyoshul Khenpo Jamyang Dorje, as well as at Delhi and Cambridge. He founded Rigpa in 1975.

Active in Buddhist studies and other fields, Soiku Shigematsu studied at Tokyo University of Foreign Studies (~1961–1965) and under Kiju Shigematsu. He held positions at Kansai Medical University (~1968–1975) and Shizuoka University (~1975–2008).
A Buddhist studies scholar, Sojo Hirano served as 助教授 at Hanazono University (attested 1974) and as 師家 at Zuigan-ji (attested 1992–1996). He taught Sonja Arntzen.

A Tibetology scholar, Solomon George FitzHerbert earned a doctorate at the University of Oxford. He served as Departmental Lecturer in Tibetan and Himalayan studies at Oxford and as a researcher at the Centre National de la Recherche Scientifique (attested 2019).

An Indologist, Somadeva Vasudeva completed a PhD at Oxford under Alexis Sanderson. He held posts at the Institut Français de Pondichéry, Columbia University as Assistant Professor of Sanskrit, and Kyoto University as Professor in 2011.

Active in Buddhist studies and philosophy, Somchai Kusalacitto earned a Ph.D. from the University of Madras. He served as dean and deputy rector for foreign affairs at Mahachulalongkornrajavidyalaya University (attested 2003).

Active in Buddhist studies and religious studies, Somphong Santacitto completed a Master's Degree in Buddhist Studies at Mahachulalongkornrajavidyalaya University under MA supervisor Phra Suthithammanuwat (attested 2006).

Specializing in Tibetology and history/archaeology, Sonam Chhoki earned an M.A. from Jawaharlal Nehru University and a Ph.D. from SOAS University of London. She served as a history teacher at Samtse College of Education.

Specializing in Tibetology and Buddhist studies, Sonam Gyatso worked as a research assistant at Toyo Bunko and as a Professor at the Central Institute of Higher Tibetan Studies (attested 2014). He taught Shinjo Kawasaki.

Sonam Kachru works in philosophy, Buddhist studies, and Indology. He earned a PhD from the University of Chicago under Dan Arnold and held posts at Chicago, the Max Planck Institute for the History of Science, and Forum Transregionale Studien.

Sonam Thakchoe, a scholar of philosophy, Buddhist studies, and Tibetology, completed a PhD at the University of Tasmania (~1999–2002) mentored by Jay L. Garfield and Jeff Malpas. He held a post at Tasmania around 2003.

Active in Tibetology and Buddhist studies, Sonam Tsering studied under doctoral supervisor Gray Tuttle, as well as teachers Khenzur Dawa, Drepung Khenzur Gyatso, Samdhong Rinpoche, Janet Gyatso, Leonard van der Kuijp, and Gyumé Khenzur Lobzang Trinlé.

Active in history, archaeology, and Buddhist studies, Songeun Choe studied under MA supervisor Myung-dae Moon and earned a PhD at the University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign under doctoral supervisor Kiyohiko Munakata (attested 1991).
Sonja Arntzen is a Japanology scholar who studied at the University of British Columbia (~1974–1979) under doctoral supervisor Leon Hurvitz, and also studied under Seizan Yanagida and Sojo Hirano.

Specializing in history, archaeology, Buddhist studies, and sinology, Sonya S. Lee earned a PhD at the University of Chicago under Wu Hung. She taught at Swarthmore College (2003–2004) and held posts at USC and Stanford.

Soon-il Hwang specializes in Buddhist studies and Indology. He earned an MA at Dongguk University under Seungwon Seo and a DPhil at Mansfield College, Oxford, under Richard Gombrich, later holding a post at Dongguk University.
Active in Buddhist studies and philosophy, Soorakkulame Pemarathana studied at the National University of Singapore under thesis supervisor Saranindranath Tagore (attested 2004).
